basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 30.' and it opens '(Vers. 30.) Et dixit Esau Jacob: da mihi gustum de coctione rubea ista, quia deficio:'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 30.) Et dixit Esau Jacob: da mihi gustum de coctione rubea ista, quia deficio: propterea vocatum est nomen ejus Edom. Rubrum, sive fulvum, lingua Hebraea EDOM (אדום) dicitur: ab eo igitur, quod rubro cibo vendiderit primitiva sua, fulvi, id est, Edom sortitus est nomen.
